sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, 2020 Revised Edition

claims.text: Clauses 30 and 41 describe a constitutional monarchy; royal signature is required for legislation. Clause 36 assigns military command to the King but requires Assembly consent for war.

The King appoints the Assembly-recommended elected representative as prime minister. Cabinet exercises executive authority collectively and answers to the Assembly; ministers are nominated by the prime minister and appointed by the King. Reserved royal powers are excluded.
The King appoints Privy Council advisers. The Council also handles specified hereditary estate and title appeals.
The Assembly includes nobles' representatives, people's representatives and Cabinet. Its recommended Speaker must be an elected nobles' representative and is appointed by the King.

sources.scope_note: Consolidated edition, not a complete amendment or commencement ledger. Do not backdate these provisions to 1990 or assume no later amendments.

sources.title: Act of Constitution of Tonga, older revised text

claims.text: The older text gives the King appointment of ministers, serving at his pleasure or for their commission period. Ministers sit in the Privy Council and Assembly.
The older text includes Privy Councillors and Cabinet in the Assembly, specifies nine noble and nine people's elected representatives, and gives the King appointment of the Speaker.

sources.scope_note: The volume carries a 1988 Revised Edition label but includes later amendment notes, including Act 12 of 1990. It is not accepted as an exact 1 January 1990 legal snapshot.

sources.title: Fatai Helu and Paula Piveni Piukala v Electoral Commission (the election of Lord Nuku), CV 55 of 2022: Ruling
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of Tonga; published by Tonga's Attorney General's Office

claims.text: The ruling refers to the PTOA party, also known as the Democratic Party; footnote 3 expands PTOA as Paati Temokalati 'a e 'Otu Motu 'Anga'ofa.
claims.uncertainty: A judicial background description, not a register entry. The court does not use the English form 'Democratic Party of the Friendly Islands' and states no registered name, founding date or legal form.

claims.text: The ruling states that the PTOA party fielded candidates for the people's representatives of a number of constituencies at the general election for which writs were issued on 2 September 2021, to be held on 18 November 2021, and that Paula Piukala was one of the candidates for Tongatapu 7.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, paragraphs 2-3; poll date also in paragraph 9 (page 2)
claims.uncertainty: attested_on is the poll date the ruling refers to; the ruling itself is dated 29 August 2022 (published_date), following this packet's convention of dating a court's event narrative by the event. Candidates formally stood as individuals; no PTOA candidate list, count or result is given.

claims.text: The ruling's background states in the present tense that Fatai Helu is the President of the party (PTOA) and that Paula Piukala is an executive member.
claims.uncertainty: A judicial background recital in a leave ruling, not a court finding: the party's officers were not in issue and no basis is given. It was probably drawn from the applicants' own filings (Piukala, named as an executive member, was an applicant), so it carries the weight of party self-description relayed by the court. No selection or appointment date, term, constitution or successor is given. Whether 'President' is the same office as party 'Leader' is not stated. 'Executive member' is not a named office.

claims.text: Self-description: the ruling relays Paula Piukala's affidavit, which supports the application filed on 17 August 2022, as stating that the objective of the PTOA is to promote the principle of equality before the law in the Kingdom. The court adds that, as evident from its mandate, the party is concerned with the election of people's representatives, and records counsel as equivocal about whether its membership includes any nobles.
claims.uncertainty: Dated by the ruling that relays it. The affidavit's own date is not given; the ruling says only that the application filed on 17 August 2022 is supported by it. The objective is a party member's own statement, labelled here as self-description; the mandate remark is the court's characterisation, not a quoted constitution.

claims.text: The proceeding is brought in the names of two individual applicants, Fatai Helu and Paula Piveni Piukala. PTOA is not named as an applicant or party, and the ruling does not describe PTOA as incorporated or registered.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, title block; whole ruling (text layer searched)
claims.uncertainty: The absence of a legal-form statement is not evidence that PTOA lacks legal personality.

sources.scope_note: Party-identity and background statements only. The application for leave was dismissed (paragraph 83), and the dismissal was upheld on appeal (AC 22 of 2022, 6 April 2023). No argument, interpretation or ruling on clause 65, and nothing about the judgment debt recited in paragraphs 1 and 4, is imported. The Attorney General's Office stamp on page 1 (28/09/22) is publication handling, not the ruling date.

sources.title: Consultation Memorandum: Seeking Stakeholder Input on a Proposed New Incorporated Societies Act
sources.publisher: Ministry of Commerce, Consumer, Trade, Innovation and Labour (MCCTIL), Tonga, with the ADB Pacific Private Sector Development Initiative

claims.text: MCCTIL states that the Incorporated Societies Act, enacted in 1988, does not support online filing. The online register it deployed in December 2025 takes filings for companies, business names, business licences and foreign-investment certification. Incorporating a society currently requires a paper application signed by five members of the proposed society, with two copies of its rules.
claims.uncertainty: Describes registry practice as at the memo date. It names no society or political party and does not say whether any political organization is registered as a society. Because the online register does not take society filings, it was not searched for PTOA.

sources.scope_note: Registry-practice evidence only; it names no society and no political party. Comments on the consultation were due 28 August 2026.

sources.title: Tonga Legislative Assembly November 2025 Election

claims.text: For the 20 November 2025 election, IPU's Candidates field reads 'Not applicable. There is no party system or candidates stood as independents.' Its 'Number of parties winning seats', 'Percentage of parties winning seats' and 'Percentage of seats won by largest party or coalition' fields also read 'Not applicable'. The 'About the election' narrative names no party and does not mention PTOA or DPFI.
claims.locator: Background, 'Candidates'; Results, 'About the election' and the three party fields
claims.uncertainty: IPU's silence states neither that PTOA won no seats nor that it won any; it supports only that IPU records no party-level result for 2025.

sources.scope_note: Live Parline page read after the cutoff for its 2025 election-description fields only; the page shows no revision date. IPU cites Legislative Assembly communications of 23 November 2025 and 23 January 2026 and news outlets. A direct non-browser request returned HTTP 403. The page's HTML changes between requests, so its response hash cannot be reproduced.

TO-DPFI-01 (tonga-dpfi-04.md): the Supreme Court (CV 55/2022, 29 August 2022) expands PTOA as Paati Temokalati 'a e 'Otu Motu 'Anga'ofa, also known as the Democratic Party, and the Court of Appeal (AC 22/2022, 6 April 2023) refers to 'PTOA or the Democratic Party'. Neither uses the English 'Democratic Party of the Friendly Islands'; the English name links to PTOA only through IPU 2021. These are court descriptions, not a register entry.

TO-DPFI-02: CV 23/2021 records evidence naming 'Mr Pohiva and the PTOA party' in the campaign after the August 2017 dissolution; reading Mr Pohiva as 'Akilisi Pohiva is contextual. With IPU 2017 this strengthens, but does not replace, the provisional grouping, and no party office for Pohiva comes from the court record.

TO-DPFI-03: founding unresolved. No founding statute, launch notice or registration instrument was found; a September 2010 launch appears only in a contemporary news report (a lead). lifecycle.from stays null.

TO-DPFI-04: legal form unresolved. None of the records searched (the judgments listed in tonga-dpfi-04.md, by text layer where one exists and visually where listed) describes PTOA as incorporated or registered, and the 2022 proceeding was brought by two individuals. Societies are filed on paper and are outside MCCTIL's online register (to_incsoc_paper_register_20260721), so a paper-register search is needed. Neither incorporation nor its absence is inferred.

TO-DPFI-05: IPU 2014 adds a second leader observation for 'Akilisi Pohiva (27 November 2014). Both leader observations are IPU-only, not Legislative Assembly, registry or court records; no continuous leadership term from 2010 to 2019 is inferred. The 2014 Assembly selection, endorsement and Cabinet claims belong to to_pm and to_cabinet.

TO-DPFI-06: 'Akilisi Pohiva's death is recorded at month precision (September 2019); the exact day needs a Prime Minister's Office release or Gazette notice. Neither Assembly article records a party-leadership transfer.

TO-DPFI-07: Fatai Helu is recited as President of the party on 29 August 2022 (role to_dpfi_president, from and until null), a judicial background recital that probably relays the applicants' filings. The party leader after September 2019 is unresolved: rival leadership claims appear only in news and tertiary leads, and no party office for 2023 to the cutoff was found in the records searched. Whether President and Leader are one office is unknown.

TO-DPFI-08: a 2025 result of no seats is not accepted. IPU 2025 records no party-level result, and the Electoral Commission's candidate list and constituency tables carry no party labels; no primary record found links any 2025 candidate to PTOA/DPFI. No dissolution or inactivity is inferred.
